text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash threatens not to go to the direct talks due to start in New York on July 9 if he is not told about the contents of a document the United Nations is due to submit to the two leaders.

- The socialist Edek party approves the candidacy of lawyer Marios Eliades, who is expected to run for the presidential elections next year with the backing of Edek, communist Akel and the centre-left United Democrats party.
- Denktash threatens to boycott talks. Turkish Cypriot leader says the UN document makes him fear a "trap".
- President Clerides says the government has no plans to suspend a proposed missile deployment in Cyprus that has outraged the Turkish side.
- Electronic shopping via the internet is on the rise in Cyprus.
- MPs are set to reveal "(money) laundering lawyers" at a parliamentary debate today.
- The United Nations is to submit thoughts and proposals on ways to solve the Cyprus problem during the direct talks between Glafcos Clerides and Rauf Denktash in New York next week.

- The political leadership in Athens and Nicosia yesterday examined three different scenarios on the stance that Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash may take during the direct talks, and the response of the Greek Cypriot side.
- The educational system in Cyprus is 30 years behind the times, says a Cyprus University professor.
- Centre-right Diko party is putting pressure on right wing Disy to support Spyros Kyprianou for the presidency next year.
- Cyprus and Greece discussed tactics the Greek Cypriot side will follow at the direct talks next week.
